title: ephemeral-surge-thicket-and-circuit-tranquilizer
author: Maya Chen

description:
Context and motivation: During a series of regional burst incidents we observed cascading circuit flips: aggressive egress bursts would exhaust cross-region egress capacity, the SLO enforcer would trip circuit breakers for affected tenants, and when capacity recovered the circuits reopened immediately causing repeat flips and sustained SLO breaches. Root cause: coarse-grained egress trimming and an immediate circuit reopen policy. Goal: reduce flip frequency and give the system a chance to settle without sacrificing tenant fairness.

What this PR does (summary): introduces a lightweight per-tenant, per-region "egress slit" (a thin, configurable carved rate) that smooths short-duration bursts at the admission edge and prevents large transient spikes from forcing immediate circuit trips. Also adds a "circuit tranquilizer" — a gentle circuit reset timer and reopen damping policy that staggers reopens and limits reopen attempts per epoch. This is implemented as a hotfix path that integrates with the existing SLO Enforcer and the edge-proxy admission flow.

Behavioral guarantees: the egress slit is best-effort and scoped to the admission edge; it never increases latency for steady-state requests beyond a few ms; default configuration is conservative to avoid impacting normal traffic; the circuit tranquilizer only delays reopen attempts (no permanent blocks) and exposes runtime knobs for canary tuning.

Implementation details: code changes live primarily in pkg/egress (egress_slit.go) and controllers/slo (enforcer.go). Key components: token bucket per-tenant-per-region, async refill worker using the existing scheduler, admission integration that prefers local slit allowance before failing fast, and a circuit reset state-machine that records reopen attempts and applies exponential calm-down with jitter. Metrics: token_consumed, slit_throttle_count, circuit_tranquilizer_delay_ms, circuit_reopen_attempts.

Testing and QA: added unit tests for token refill and fairness (pkg/egress/egress_slit_test.go), integration test for admission success/fail cases during bursts (controllers/slo/enforcer_test.go), and a synthetic canary manifest under helm/values/staging.yaml. Local microbenchmarks show admission p95 increases by <=1.8ms under the conservative default config.

Rollout plan: staged canary in us-west-2 with 5% edge-proxy fleet, monitor slit_throttle_count and circuit_reopen_attempts for 24 hours, then 25% / 100% if stable. Immediate backout: flip helm flag egress.slit.enabled=false and circuit.tranquilizer.enabled=false; the enforcer will revert to pre-hotfix behavior.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added and passing
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Canary manifest included
- [x] Telemetry definitions added
- [x] Ops doc and rollout notes (docs/ops/egress-slit.md)
- [x] Approved by on-call SRE

CI summary: initial CI run had a flaky timeout on egress_slit_test (race against timeouts) — test timeout increased from 200ms to 500ms in the test harness; subsequent runs passed. All other checks (build, lint, go vet, integration) passed.

Migration/backport: This was cherry-picked and applied as a hotfix branch for the active incident window. Backport notes are in the Linear ticket (ENG-1329).

Why this is different from previous load-shedding approaches: instead of coarse global shedding that can disconnect tenants abruptly, the slit is a fine-grained admission shaping primitive that buys time for the SLO enforcer to make more informed decisions. The circuit tranquilizer prevents reopen thrash rather than adding severe penalties on initial trip.

Risks and mitigations: incorrect token accounting could unfairly throttle heavy tenants — mitigated by conservative defaults and reserve bucket for background tasks. Another risk is hidden latency increase; mitigated by microbenchmarks and a conservative canary rollout.

Related tickets: ENG-1329 (primary), ENG-1340 (follow-up to expose tuning knobs in Redwood Console), SUP-7723 (incident case).
